title: Encoded output lookup run
statement: Let $C,e,p,B$ be natural numbers, let $m$ be a Boolean mode, let $f$ map finite bit strings to finite bit strings, let $x,b$ be finite bit strings, and let $v$ assign a natural number to each of fourteen registers. Suppose every register value is at most $B$, register $0$ is $0$, register $3$ is twice the length of the encoding of $(x,b)$, register $4$ is $4|x|+4$, register $11$ is twice the length of $f(x)$, register $13$ is $0$, and register $5$ is $p$. Suppose also that the encoding of $(f(x),b)$ has length at most $B$. Then, from the seek state on the nested encoding of $(x,b)$ with binary index $p$, register vector $v$, and no answer, the computation halts with answer equal to the Boolean that is true exactly when $p$ is less than the length of the encoding of $(f(x),b)$ if $m$ is true, and otherwise equal to the bit at position $p$ of that encoding, with out-of-range positions interpreted as false. Every configuration before halting satisfies the program’s instruction-side conditions and register bound $B$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps finite bit strings to finite bit strings
$v$ assigns natural-number values to fourteen registers
Every register value is at most $B$
Register $3$ equals twice the length of the encoding of $(x,b)$
Register $11$ equals twice the length of $f(x)$

replaced:
Let $C,e$ be natural numbers, let $m$ be a Boolean mode, let $f$ be a function on bit
strings, let $x,b$ be bit strings, let $p,B$ be natural numbers, and let $v$ assign
natural-number counters to the fourteen registers. Suppose every counter is at most $B$,
and the counters satisfy: register $0$ is $0$; register $3$ is twice the length of the
encoding of $(x,b)$; register $4$ is $4|x|+4$; register $11$ is twice $|f(x)|$; register
$13$ is $0$; and register $5$ is $p$. Also suppose the encoding of $(f(x),b)$ has length
at most $B$. Then the specified computation, started on the nested encoding of $(x,b)$
with binary index $p$, in its seek state with counters $v$ and no answer yet, halts with
answer true exactly when $p$ is less than the length of the encoding of $(f(x),b)$ if
$m$ is true; otherwise it halts with the bit at position $p$ of that encoding, using
false for an out-of-range position. Every configuration before halting satisfies the
machine's instruction-side conditions and register bound $B$.
